Hal Tolley.narrative: I farm the old Coldwell fields on the Guild's lease, and I've earned every furrow. The Hales had their chance to stay and pay like the rest of us; they chose outlawry instead. Now they come to the field edge at night, and I'm done waiting for Mercy Abbot's stone. I keep my son watching from the barn and my wife behind the door.
goals: Get a stone wall built around the yard
Keep the Hales off the fields
Make the farm pay enough to keep the lease
See my children safe and settled
Teach Tib to plough a straight furrow and read the weather
Get a stone wall built around the yard, one load at a time

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: landlord
relations.note: She holds the lease I farm, but she's left me to face the Hales alone.

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: threat
relations.note: She wants these fields back, and I won't give them up.

relations.name: Marta Tolley
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the house and wants a wall as much as I do.

relations.name: Tib Tolley
relations.label: son
relations.note: He watches from the barn and knows the fields as well as I do.

relations.name: Nell Tolley
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She's afraid of the woods, and I can't blame her.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: reeve
relations.note: He took the fields from the Hales and let them to the Guild; I just farm them.

relations.name: Osbert Ashby
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A good neighbour; he sells grain and keeps to his own.

relations.name: Ned Hale
relations.label: outlaw
relations.note: He's the one who does the threatening on the road.

relations.name: Hob Ferrier
relations.label: outlaw
relations.note: He's been at the field edge with Ned, looking at my barn.

memories.gist: The day I signed the lease with Mercy Abbot for the old Coldwell fields, thinking I'd finally have land of my own.
Seeing Ned Hale and Hob Ferrier at the edge of the field at dusk, just standing and looking.
Asking Mercy Abbot for stone to build a wall, and getting nothing but words.
The Lean Year, when the blight came and we all went hungry until the town store lent grain.
Teaching Tib to watch from the barn and count the men in the woods.

stances.why: The Guild leased them to me fair and square, and I've worked them.
They refused to give up their houses and took to the road; that makes them outlaws.
Words won't stop men at night; stone will.
My wife and children are all I've got.
I pay rent to the Guild; they should keep me safe.

pastimes: walking his field boundaries at first light, checking the furrows and the hedges
mending harness and tools by the barn door in the evening
sitting with Marta and the children at the hearth after supper, listening to Tib's day
Hal Tolley.calling: I farm the old Coldwell fields on the Guild's lease, and I've earned every furrow of them.
